entries.reason: The operator's own policy directory. Truthful on purpose so a test can name the file it must not touch; DEF-042/110. `PolicyStore.live` is the seam that keeps a test process off it.

Where a capture lands when the caller names no path. Writer. DEF-142: four PNGs per run went into the operator's own captures from PRO-0089 until the REQ-055 witness caught it. The operator literal is inside this declaration's own guard.

A pure path builder: the root arrives as an argument, so this declaration cannot reach the operator by itself. Its two un-argued callers, `operatorURL` and `defaultURL`, carry the classification.

PRO-0099. The host end of a forwarded guest socket. Connected to, never created: `Proctor never opens the tunnel: a socket nothing is listening on is a refusal, not an attempt to create one`. It also already takes `home` as an argument, so a caller that names its own root has a seam.

PRO-0099. The reflector's bind path — `reflector-<pid>.sock`, pid-named, unlinked, carrying no operator data. Classed socket over the out-of-family verdict, which called it a writer because bind(2) creates an inode; the deciding facts are that the only caller of the bare `start()` is ProctorUIApp, the suite's ReflectorWitnessTests already passes an explicit path, and ProctorReflector is a zero-dependency library PRODUCT that other packages embed, so reaching a test-process predicate would mean either a new dependency edge for every consumer or a second copy of the predicate. `operator_path_gate.py` guard `no_bare_reflector_start` is what keeps the parameter seam load-bearing instead of remembered.
PRO-0099. Three lines of copy on the TUI's `Reaching the agent` screen — a string a person reads, telling them where the socket is. Nothing resolves it.

PRO-0099. Two JSON-schema `description` strings for the guest tool's `remoteSocket` and `localSocket` arguments, saying where each default lives. Prose in a tool description, read by a model, resolved by nothing.

no_bare_reflector_start.reason: PRO-0099. ProctorReflector.supportDirectory is classed `socket` partly because the suite always passes an explicit path. That is a fact about the tests rather than about the code, so it is checked rather than trusted: a bare `ProctorReflector.start()` anywhere under Tests/ would bind `reflector-<pid>.sock` into the operator's own root, and this refuses it.

_predicates: The bare spelling is here because AuditLog.directory writes  from inside AuditLog itself. A predicate is only counted on a line of code — code_only() drops comments — so a doc comment naming one cannot satisfy a seam.
